about: Lawful public sources the radar's monitoring layer reads, each through its own public pages as a person would read them: never behind a sign-in, through a VPN or under a hidden identity. Each lists the page that sets its terms and what they allow, as read on 22 October 2026, a standing reliability grade (A to F), and how often to read it. fd-core's monitor module checks every item against this file before it is filed.

sources.name: GOV.UK: UK sanctions on Russia (news and sanctions notices)
sources.terms_note: Open Government Licence v3.0 (GOV.UK). Notices name designated persons: items carry no names, only counts, countries of address and kinds of goods

sources.name: Ministry of Trade of Türkiye: monthly foreign trade data
sources.publisher: Ministry of Trade, Republic of Türkiye
sources.terms_note: Site footer: all rights reserved; no reuse terms stated. Items keep a short excerpt with the link for internal monitoring; anything shared beyond that needs the publisher's permission [Likely]

sources.name: National Statistical Committee of the Kyrgyz Republic: news
sources.publisher: National Statistical Committee of the Kyrgyz Republic
sources.terms_note: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA 4.0 (the licensing page, read 22 Oct 2026): attribution, no commercial use, share-alike, changes stated. The site footer also requires citing the source (Law on Official Statistics, article 30) and carries an all rights reserved notice. Fine for internal monitoring with attribution; a paid deployment or wider sharing needs the committee's permission
